cells.tense: You are keeping the exchange fair in the present, and giving and taking move in turn without strain.
cells.ask: This week, when you hand something over, name plainly what you'd want back. Let the answer arrive without steering it.
cells.core:
This is an exchange running clean. You hand something over and something comes back, and the two aren't far apart. Around you a false arrangement already came apart, and in the room it left, fairness comes easier than it did — you don't tally ahead, you don't wait to see whether you'll come up short before you commit.

What that looks like when it's going well: you notice what's on the table, you put your half down, you let theirs land where it lands. Evenness like this holds weight too — it feeds whatever you build next, and it does so quietly. One cost, small and steady. Keeping a trade even asks for regular attention; it doesn't run in the background, and nobody is going to keep it even on your behalf.

cells.verb: trading fairly with what's actually there — giving and taking in turn

cells.tense: You are bracing for a reckoning that has not arrived, paying accounts before the debt is real.
cells.ask: Pick one exchange you're over-managing. Pay your half simple, then leave their half alone for a week.
cells.core:
You're ahead of the fairness. Nobody has asked anything of you yet, and you've already worked out what you owe, what they owe, how it all evens out — the arithmetic has crowded the exchange itself off the table. The space a clearing opened is full of imagined ledgers.

Sighted, this is plain clear perception: you can tell what's fair without running the numbers. The bend is that the running has replaced the trading. You can't swap anything with someone whose ending you've written, and you can't receive what you've already priced. Keep your footing without clamping shut — give the half you decide to give, take what's held out to you, let the rest show up on its own schedule.

cells.tense: You went quiet on the giving and the taking, and the cleared space sits unused in front of you.
cells.ask: Make one small, specific offer to one person today. Leave the receiving side alone and let it answer itself.
cells.core:
Turned the other way, this is a plain open hand: you set something down, you pick something up, and neither direction costs more than it should. That is an even exchange, and it is available in this cleared space. Where you stand, both hands are still. Offering and receiving went quiet at once — putting something out feels like standing exposed, taking something in feels like a debt starting — so you hold off on both and file it as keeping things simple.

Sharp attention is what would move it, not nerve and not generosity: noticing what's actually on the table in front of you rather than the version you've assumed is there. Offer one thing you can afford to lose.

cells.tense: You are already keeping the exchange even while you file it under luck or the other person's good nature.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did to even a recent exchange, out loud, and say plainly that you did it.
cells.core:
Running well, this works like a reflex with eyes on it: a trade tips, and you move to correct it — a smaller gesture, an equal turn, a give that answers a take — and the correction lands before you've reasoned it through. You are doing that, often enough that it's part of how you already move through a room.

The bend is attribution. Afterward the credit goes to circumstance: they were generous, the timing lined up, things fell that way. It reads as modesty. It also means the part you played gets filed under conditions you didn't set. Nothing about the way you do this needs repair. One sentence said plainly, to one person, marks the move as yours.
